chronology_issues.subject: Creation, Ur-Dragon, earliest Elder Dragons
chronology_issues.uncertainty_note: Mythic accounts and enormous approximate spans do not form a precise calendar.
chronology_issues.editorial_treatment: Use “tradition,” “account,” and broad relative placement; never invent a creation date.

chronology_issues.subject: Cross-plane simultaneity
chronology_issues.uncertainty_note: AR is Dominarian and most planes lack a convertible calendar.
chronology_issues.editorial_treatment: Say “before,” “after,” or “by the time”; avoid synchronized years unless a primary source supplies them.

chronology_issues.subject: Legends-era Dominaria
chronology_issues.uncertainty_note: Early cards, licensed comics, and later novels leave gaps or shift emphasis.
chronology_issues.editorial_treatment: Keep Madara and Jamuraa in bounded chronicles and cite the version used.

chronology_issues.subject: The Thran and Artifact Cycle
chronology_issues.uncertainty_note: Core causal detail is novel-led and was published after the earliest card sets.
chronology_issues.editorial_treatment: Use novels as narrative backbone, cards as depicted evidence, and later summaries as retcon checks.

chronology_issues.subject: The Dark, Fallen Empires, Homelands, Mirage
chronology_issues.uncertainty_note: Significant portions are fragmentary, old-periodical, comic, or card-only.
chronology_issues.editorial_treatment: Do a primary-source packet before any script; use lower-confidence language.

chronology_issues.subject: Karona’s planar meetings
chronology_issues.uncertainty_note: Several apparent meetings conflict with later dating or characterization.
chronology_issues.editorial_treatment: Present them as disputed or unreliable experiences, not settled travel chronology.

chronology_issues.subject: Planar Chaos
chronology_issues.uncertainty_note: Alternate figures are possibilities entering the main timeline.
chronology_issues.editorial_treatment: Label every alternate self on screen; do not rewrite mainline biographies.

chronology_issues.subject: The Mending
chronology_issues.uncertainty_note: Outcomes are established, but a single exhaustive mechanism and synchronized instant across all worlds are not.
chronology_issues.editorial_treatment: Explain confirmed changes to power and travel, then mark inference.

chronology_issues.subject: Test of Metal
chronology_issues.uncertainty_note: Its time-travel and continuity are widely treated as conflicting with the surrounding story.
chronology_issues.editorial_treatment: Keep outside the core spine until a source-by-source canon ruling is documented.

chronology_issues.subject: Scars block novels
chronology_issues.uncertainty_note: Characterization and connective events require reconciliation with later official summaries.
chronology_issues.editorial_treatment: Script only after comparing the novel, cards, and current retrospective text.

chronology_issues.subject: Theros Beyond Death
chronology_issues.uncertainty_note: No full conventional story was published; much must be reconstructed from cards and summaries.
chronology_issues.editorial_treatment: The included reconstruction arc must use a card-and-summary audit and must not invent a missing novel.

chronology_issues.subject: Ikoria
chronology_issues.uncertainty_note: The novel and cards differ on important creature identity/fate details.
chronology_issues.editorial_treatment: State each presentation and any later official resolution.

chronology_issues.subject: War of the Spark and Forsaken
chronology_issues.uncertainty_note: Sources and later fiction create disputed relationship and characterization beats.
chronology_issues.editorial_treatment: Separate event sequence from contested characterization; quote minimally and cite precisely.

chronology_issues.subject: March of the Machine
chronology_issues.uncertainty_note: Many fronts overlap without a complete universal clock.
chronology_issues.editorial_treatment: Group episodes by causal front and characters; do not intercut merely to simulate simultaneity.

chronology_issues.subject: Universes Beyond
